middle-point.question: For the points $(1,2),\ (2,4),\ (3,5),\ (4,4),\ (5,5)$ the fitted line has $\hat\beta_1=0.6$ and $\hat\beta_0=2.2$. Move the point $(3,5)$ straight up by 2 units, to $(3,7)$. What happens to the slope and the intercept?
options: The slope increases and the intercept decreases
The slope increases and the intercept stays at 2.2
The slope stays at 0.6 and the intercept rises to 2.6
middle-point.explanation: The point sits at $x=3=\bar x$, so its term in $S_{xy}=\sum(x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)$ is $0$ times something, whatever its height. Moving it changes neither $S_{xy}$ nor $S_{xx}$, so the slope stays at $0.6$. It does raise $\bar y$ from $4$ to $4.4$, and the line still passes through $(\bar x,\bar y)$ with the same slope, so the intercept rises from $4-0.6\times3=2.2$ to $4.4-0.6\times3=2.6$. A point far from $\bar x$ would tilt the line instead.
